LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 8.1.1 SONGS/ORAL POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg
Topic 8.1: Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry, part of Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do the initiation songs propagate promotion of culture?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the features of initiation songs for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the subject matter and functions of a given initiation song,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform an initiation song for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the significance of initiation songs in promoting culture.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 8.1.1 Songs/Oral Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

1. identify the features of initiation songs for information,
2. analyse the subject matter and functions of a given initiation song,
3. perform an initiation song for effective communication,
4. acknowledge the significance of initiation songs in promoting culture.

Remember the key question: How do the initiation songs propagate promotion of culture?
